final_answer:
Short answer: No. On these facts the Lease is very likely a 'finance lease' under Virginia's UCC Article 2A, so Client cannot stop paying Lessor because of the defective Trailers, and Lessor is not responsible for them. Client's remedy is against Manufacturer (here, a claim in the Chapter 7 case).

1. Finance lease status. Va. Code 8.2A-103(1)(g) defines a finance lease as one where (i) the lessor does not select, manufacture or supply the goods; (ii) the lessor acquires the goods in connection with the lease; and (iii) one of several alternatives occurs, including that the lessee receives a copy of the supply contract before signing the lease. Here Client picked the model and negotiated specs directly with Manufacturer; Lessor merely bought the Trailers and financed them (Lessor did not select, manufacture or supply); Lessor bought the Trailers for the lease; and Client got the complete purchase agreement, including the warranty, before signing. Client's own selection and negotiation does not defeat finance-lease status; it supports it. This is a commercial lease, so the consumer-lease carve-outs do not apply.

2. Hell-or-high-water. Under 8.2A-407, for a finance lease that is not a consumer lease, the lessee's promises become irrevocable and independent on acceptance of the goods, and are not subject to cancellation, termination, modification, repudiation, excuse or substitution without the consent of the party to whom the promise runs. The Lease's 'absolute and unconditional, irrespective of any defense or setoff' clause is consistent with and reinforced by the statute. Client accepted and used the Trailers for four months. The compressor failures arose after delivery and do not by themselves excuse payment. Client's non-payment is therefore a lessee default, exposing it to Lessor's default remedies under Article 2A Part 5 (acceleration if the lease so provides, repossession, disposition, damages, and contractual fees). I did not verify the text of those remedy sections or any Virginia case law.

3. No lessor warranty liability. Implied warranties of merchantability (8.2A-212) and fitness (8.2A-213) are expressly inapplicable to finance leases, and the Lease contains no Lessor warranty and routes claims to Manufacturer.

4. Client's recourse. Under 8.2A-209, the benefit of the supplier's warranties (including the two-year warranty) extends to Client to the extent of its leasehold interest, subject to the warranty's terms and defenses; Client also keeps rights against Manufacturer under other law. Client should give prompt notice of default to Manufacturer (and Lessor) under 8.2A-516(3)-type notice rules (reasonable time after discovery; the Manufacturer already agreed to fix, which helps). Because Manufacturer is in Chapter 7, Client should file a proof of claim for warranty/damages (consider also whether third-party warranty or insurance, or any component supplier warranty such as the compressor maker, is available). The trustee's refusal to honor warranty claims leaves Client as an unsecured creditor, likely recovering little. This does not shift the loss to Lessor.

5. Caveats and risks. (a) Finance-lease status depends on the facts stated; if Lessor in fact selected or supplied the Trailers, or made its own warranties/representations, the analysis changes. (b) Hell-or-high-water enforcement could be challenged on unconscionability (8.2A-108) or fraud/bad faith, which seems unlikely on these facts. (c) Mutual agreement: Client may negotiate with Lessor (workout, assignment of warranty claims, replacement units), but Lessor has no duty to agree. (d) Client's practical advice: resume payments (or cure) promptly to avoid acceleration and default remedies; consider reserving rights against Manufacturer estate; check the Lease's default, acceleration, late-fee and attorney's fee clauses and any guaranties. (e) The Virginia Code site was blocked from direct fetching; statute text was confirmed through search-result summaries only, and no case law was located or verified within budget. Revocation of acceptance against a finance lessor (8.2A-517) is limited in effect because 8.2A-407 makes the rent promise independent; I did not independently verify the treatment in Virginia cases.

authorities.title: Definitions - finance lease
authorities.proposition: Finance lease: lessor does not select, manufacture or supply goods; acquires goods in connection with lease; and lessee receives supply contract copy before signing (among alternatives).

authorities.title: Irrevocable promises: finance leases
authorities.proposition: In a non-consumer finance lease, lessee's promises become irrevocable and independent on acceptance; not subject to cancellation, termination, modification, repudiation, excuse or substitution without consent.

authorities.title: Lessee under finance lease as beneficiary of supply contract
authorities.proposition: Supplier's warranties extend to finance lessee to extent of leasehold interest; lessee retains other rights against supplier.

authorities.title: Implied warranties
authorities.proposition: Implied warranties of merchantability and fitness apply 'except in a finance lease'.

authorities.title: Effect of acceptance; notice of default
authorities.proposition: After acceptance lessee must notify lessor and supplier within a reasonable time of discovering default or be barred from remedies against the party not notified.

claims.text: The Lease is a finance lease under Virginia Article 2A.
Client's rent obligation is irrevocable and independent after acceptance; Client cannot lawfully withhold payment because of the Trailer defects.
Lessor is not liable for the defective Trailers (no implied warranties in finance lease; no express warranty in Lease).
Client's remedy is against Manufacturer via warranty benefits under 8.2A-209, e.g., a claim in the Chapter 7 case, with timely notice.
